verses.93:2: Exaltai-vos, vós que julgais a terra: * pagai a retribuição aos soberbos.
verses.93:3: Até quando os pecadores, Senhor, * até quando os pecadores se gloriarão?
verses.93:4: Proferirão, e falarão iniquidade: * falarão todos os que praticam a injustiça?
verses.93:5: Humilharam, Senhor, o vosso povo: * e {vexaverunt} a vossa herança.
verses.93:6: {interfecerunt} a viúva e o forasteiro: * e {occiderunt}.
verses.93:7: E disseram: O Senhor não verá, * nem entenderá o Deus de Jacó.
verses.93:9: {qui9a} plantou o ouvido não ouvirá? * ou {qui9b} formou o olho não {considerat}?
verses.93:10: {qui10a} castiga as nações não repreenderá, * {qui10b} ensina ao homem o saber?
verses.93:11: O Senhor conhece os pensamentos dos homens, * {quoniam}.
verses.93:12: Bem-aventurado o homem a quem vós instruirdes, Senhor, * e a quem ensinardes {delege},
verses.93:13: {mitiges}: * até que se cave o fosso para o pecador.
verses.93:14: Porque o Senhor não repelirá o seu povo: * e não abandonará a sua herança.
verses.93:16: Quem se levantará por mim contra os malvados? * ou quem {stabit} contra os que praticam a iniquidade?
verses.93:17: Se o Senhor não me tivesse auxiliado, * {paulo}.
verses.93:18: Se eu dizia: O meu pé {motus}: * a vossa misericórdia, Senhor, me auxiliava.
verses.93:19: Segundo a multidão das minhas dores no meu coração, * as vossas consolações alegraram a minha alma.
verses.93:20: Acaso {adhaeret} o trono da iniquidade, * vós que {fingis}?
verses.93:21: {captabunt} do justo: * e condenarão o sangue inocente.
verses.93:22: E o Senhor se fez refúgio para mim: * e o meu Deus, auxílio da minha esperança.
verses.93:23: E lhes pagará a iniquidade deles, e na malícia deles {disperdet1}: * {disperdet2} o Senhor, nosso Deus.

decisions.why: A verbless sentence of two nouns: which is subject? The Latin's order puts 'Deus ultiónum' first, and the second colon begins with the same words, so keeping the order keeps the anaphora the verse is built on. 'O Senhor é o Deus das vinganças' (MS1932, DRB) is the plainer statement but moves the repeated words off the head of the verse. The copula is supplied either way (grammar, D2). Plural 'vinganças' kept, as ultiónum (ἐκδικήσεων).

options.label: O Deus das vinganças é o Senhor

forms.v1a: O Deus das vinganças é o Senhor

options.note: Ruling: the Latin's order; both colons open 'o Deus das vinganças'.

options.label: O Senhor é o Deus das vinganças

forms.v1a: O Senhor é o Deus das vinganças

options.note: MS1932, DRB ('The Lord is the God to whom revenge belongeth'); the plainer order, the anaphora loosened.

options.label: O Deus da vingança é o Senhor

forms.v1a: O Deus da vingança é o Senhor

options.note: Singular, as MS1932 and most modern ears expect; drops the Latin's plural — then the second colon should follow ('o Deus da vingança').

decisions.why: ἐπαρρησιάσατο: acted (or spoke) boldly, openly. The Latin says 'acted freely'; DRB 'hath acted freely', MS1932 'agiu livremente'. 'abertamente' is the Greek's sense, not the Latin's word.

options.label: agiu livremente
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's two words; DRB, MS1932.

options.label: agiu com liberdade
options.note: same sense, a noun for the adverb; ends oxytone.

options.label: agiu abertamente
options.note: the Greek's παρρησία; refused as the Greek's sense, not the Latin's word (rule 1).

decisions.why: The cognate 'vexar' in Brazil means to humiliate or embarrass — a false friend, and 'humilhar' is already in the first colon. The Greek is ἐκάκωσαν (did evil to, maltreated); the same Latin verb returns at 105:32 (Moses) and 106:39, both κακόω. 'afligir' is taken by afflígere (glossary, 16:8b).

options.label: maltrataram
options.note: Ruling: the verb's sense (κακόω), free in the glossary, and fits 105:32 and 106:39.

options.label: afligiram
options.note: DRB 'afflicted'; collides with afflígere → afligir.

options.label: oprimiram
options.note: MS1932; opprímere's word, not this one.

decisions.why: Two Latin verbs for killing, and the Portuguese should have two. occídere is 'matar' everywhere else in the psalter (77:31, 34, 47; 104:29 fish, 77:47 vines; 134:10, 135:18, 138:19 — grep), where 'assassinar' is impossible; so occídere keeps 'matar' and interfícere (only here) takes the other verb. The Greek has the gradation the other way round (ἀπέκτειναν … ἐφόνευσαν, killed … murdered; DRB 'slain … murdered'), which option 2 follows.

options.label: Assassinaram … mataram
options.note: Ruling: occídere keeps the psalter's 'matar'; the two Latin verbs stay two.

options.label: Mataram … assassinaram
options.note: the Greek's and DRB's gradation (killed … murdered); breaks occídere → matar.

options.label: Mataram … tiraram a vida aos órfãos
options.note: MS1932 ('tiraram a vida aos órfãos'): a paraphrase for the second verb.

decisions.why: insípiens → insensato and stultus → tolo are settled (D43). 'in pópulo' is 'among the people': 'do povo' (MS1932) is the natural Portuguese, 'entre o povo' hugs the preposition. 'aliquándo' (ποτέ) is 'at some time, at last' (DRB 'at last'); 'sápere' is the verb of sápiens, so 'sede sábios'. 'vós' supplied so that the vocative is heard as one (grammar).

options.label: do povo … sede sábios enfim
options.note: Ruling.

options.label: entre o povo … sede sábios enfim
options.note: the Latin's 'in' kept; DRB 'among the people'.

options.label: do povo … sede sábios um dia
options.note: aliquándo as 'some day' — the other half of its range.

options.label: do povo … sede finalmente prudentes
options.note: MS1932; 'prudente' is prudens's word.

decisions.latin: Qui plantávit … qui finxit … Qui córripit … qui docet
decisions.why: Four relatives with no antecedent, two per verse. 'Quem' is the Portuguese headless relative and keeps each colon near the Latin's length (93:10a: 12 syllables against 'Aquele que…' 15, Latin 10). The risk is that 'Quem' is heard as interrogative ('Who planted the ear [and] will not hear?'); the question mark on the main verb decides it. MS1932 has 'aquele que … o que'.

options.label: Quem … quem
options.note: Ruling: short, the fourfold repetition kept.

options.label: Aquele que … aquele que
options.note: cannot be heard as a question word; +2 to +5 syllables a colon.

decisions.why: consideráre is 'considerar' for things (118:15, 18) and 'observar' with a person as object (21:18, 36:32). Here it has no object; κατανοεῖ, 'perceive, observe'. 'não considera?' is heard as 'does he not take into account?' — a mental act, where the verse is about the eye. Present tense kept (against 'ouvirá'), as the Latin has it.

options.label: observa
options.note: Ruling: the eye's verb, and the glossary's second word for consideráre.

options.label: considera
options.note: the glossary's first word; heard as judging more than seeing.

options.label: verá
options.note: MS1932 — another verb and tense.

decisions.why: quóniam (ὅτι) after 'scit' is 'that' (DRB 'that they are vain'; 1 Cor 3:20 quotes the verse — from memory, unverified); it could also be read 'because'. 'que são vãos' reads first as a relative ('the thoughts, which are vain'), which says the same thing and keeps both readings audible.

options.label: que são vãos
options.note: Ruling: DRB's 'that'; open as the Latin.

options.label: e sabe que são vãos
options.note: MS1932's gloss ('ele sabe') made text: an addition.

options.label: porque são vãos
options.note: the causal reading; decides what the Latin leaves open.

decisions.latin: et de lege tua docúeris eum
decisions.why: 'de lege' (ἐκ τοῦ νόμου) is 'out of your law' (DRB): the law is the source of the teaching. 'da vossa lei' keeps the preposition; 'na vossa lei' (MS1932 'amestrares na tua lei') is smoother but makes the law the subject taught. The resumptive 'eum' is a Hebraism Portuguese does not repeat ('a quem … e a quem'). Latin 'Beátus homo, quem tu erudíeris, Dómine' is read alone as a Matins versicle (Psalmi matutinum) — the first colon stands alone.

options.label: da vossa lei
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's 'de'.

options.label: pela vossa lei
options.note: the law as the means.

options.label: na vossa lei
options.note: MS1932; the law as the matter taught.

decisions.latin: Ut mítiges ei a diébus malis
decisions.why: mitigáre → abrandar (glossary, 84:4, its only other place). The Latin is compressed: 'that you may soften (things) for him, away from the evil days' (πραΰναι αὐτῷ ἀφ' ἡμερῶν πονηρῶν; DRB 'give him rest from the evil days'). Portuguese 'abrandar' needs an object; the ruling makes 'os dias maus' its object (as MS1932 'suavizar os dias maus'), which loses 'a' but keeps the verb and the dative. 'aliviar de' keeps the 'from' but changes the verb.

options.label: Para que lhe abrandeis os dias maus

forms.mitiges: Para que lhe abrandeis os dias maus

options.note: Ruling: glossary verb; 'a' absorbed into the object (grammar).

options.label: Para o aliviardes dos dias maus

forms.mitiges: Para o aliviardes dos dias maus

options.note: keeps 'a diébus' as 'dos'; another verb than 84:4.

options.label: Para lhe dardes descanso dos dias maus

forms.mitiges: Para lhe dardes descanso dos dias maus

options.note: DRB's 'give him rest' (the Greek's calming); a paraphrase of the verb.

decisions.why: 'convértere in' with a thing is a change of nature → 'converter em' (glossary row, 65:6, 77:44): justice turned into judgment (DRB 'be turned into judgment'). The Greek ἐπιστρέψῃ εἰς κρίσιν can be 'return to judgment', which 'se volte para o juízo' would say. The Latin 'in' + accusative holds both; the ruling follows the Vulgate-family reading and the glossary row.

options.label: se converta em juízo
options.note: Ruling: DRB; the glossary's 'converter em'.

options.label: se volte para o juízo
options.note: the Greek's 'return to'; convértere's usual 'voltar'.

decisions.latin: et qui juxta illam omnes qui recto sunt corde
decisions.why: The colon has no verb: 'and those near it — all who are upright of heart'. DRB supplies 'are' (a statement: those near justice are the upright); MS1932 supplies a subjunctive under 'até que' ('e estejam perto dela todos'). The ruling supplies only the verb of the relative and leaves the two groups in apposition, as the Latin does, so both readings stay open.

options.label: e os que estão junto dela, todos os retos de coração

forms.juxta: e os que estão junto dela, todos os retos de coração

options.note: Ruling: verbless apposition kept; 'retos de coração' the glossary's formula.

options.label: e os que estão junto dela são todos os retos de coração

forms.juxta: e os que estão junto dela são todos os retos de coração

options.note: DRB's statement.

options.label: e estejam junto dela todos os retos de coração

forms.juxta: e estejam junto dela todos os retos de coração

options.note: MS1932's subjunctive, dependent on 'Até que'.

decisions.why: stare → estar de pé (glossary, open; 23:3 'quem estará de pé no seu lugar santo?'). Here it is standing beside a man against enemies — the posture of a fighter, which 'estar de pé' keeps; it costs two syllables in a long colon (+4 against the Latin).

options.label: estará de pé comigo
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's word, as 23:3.

options.label: se manterá comigo
options.note: shorter; 'hold firm with me'.

options.label: estará comigo
options.note: MS1932; the posture lost.

decisions.latin: paulo minus habitásset in inférno ánima mea
decisions.why: 'Nisi quia' + perfect, then a pluperfect subjunctive: an unreal condition (DRB, MS1932 both counterfactual; 118:92 is built the same way, D24). 'paulo minus' is 'almost' → 'por pouco' (118:87). The ruling keeps the conditional and the Latin's order, the soul last. Brazilian idiom says 'por pouco … não' with a past indicative (118:87 'Por pouco não acabaram comigo'); after an unreal 'Se' the conditional is the grammatical match. inférnus → inferno (glossary, open; heard as hell of the damned first — the row is for Gustavo).

options.label: por pouco teria habitado no inferno a minha alma

forms.paulo: por pouco teria habitado no inferno a minha alma

options.note: Ruling.

options.label: por pouco a minha alma não habitou no inferno

forms.paulo: por pouco a minha alma não habitou no inferno

options.note: the idiom of 118:87; mood changed.

options.label: por pouco teria habitado na mansão dos mortos a minha alma

forms.paulo: por pouco teria habitado na mansão dos mortos a minha alma

options.note: the inferno row's option (unverified Creed wording); a paraphrase.

decisions.why: movéri → ser abalado; the glossary row names this verse, and 37:17 'enquanto os meus pés são abalados', 16:5 and 72:2 already say it of feet. 65:9 'não deixou vacilar os meus pés' is a noun phrase (in commotiónem). Kept for the family; 'vacilou' is the more natural image for a foot.

options.label: foi abalado
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's verb, as 37:17, 72:2.

options.label: vacilou
options.note: MS1932 'está vacilante'; the row's option.

decisions.why: adhærére → apegar-se a (glossary, open), 'colar-se' for bodies. Here the throne of iniquity 'cleaving to' God — being joined to him (συμπροσέσται σοι, 'shall it be in league with you?'). 'se apega a vós' keeps the Latin's image of clinging; 'se une a vós' is plainer and says the alliance. numquid → acaso (glossary); sedes → trono (θρόνος; glossary for God's seat — here its counterfeit), against MS1932's 'cadeira'.

options.label: se apega a vós
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's verb.

options.label: se une a vós
options.note: the sense (alliance), another verb.

options.label: tem parte convosco
options.note: close to MS1932 'tem alguma coisa de comum contigo'; a paraphrase.

decisions.why: The obscurest colon of the psalm. The Latin is second person — God is the one 'who fashions labour in the commandment' (DRB 'who framest labour in commandment'; MS1932 'contigo que nos impões mandamentos penosos') — where the Greek's participle belongs to the throne. fíngere → formar (glossary; the same verb as 93:9 'formou o olho', which the psalm echoes), labor → fadiga (glossary), præcéptum → decreto (settled, D19, which names this verse). 'vós que' makes the address audible. Left as dark as the Latin; no gloss.

options.label: formais a fadiga no decreto
options.note: Ruling: the three glossary words, the Latin's 'in'.

options.label: formais a fadiga pelo decreto
options.note: ἐπὶ προστάγματι read as 'by decree'.

options.label: nos impondes decretos penosos
options.note: MS1932's interpretation; refused (rule 2: explains).

decisions.why: captáre in (θηρεύσουσιν ἐπί) is to hunt after, try to catch (DRB 'They will hunt after the soul of the just'). The cognate 'captar' means to pick up a signal. 'Darão caça a' is the Portuguese idiom for hunting down and keeps the Latin's 'in' as 'a'.

options.label: Darão caça à alma
options.note: Ruling.

options.label: Caçarão a alma
options.note: one verb, the preposition dropped.

options.label: Armarão laços à alma
options.note: MS1932 — an image the Latin does not have.

decisions.why: The psalm ends by repeating the verb across the asterisk (anadiplosis). dispérdere → exterminar (glossary). Brazilian speech accepts the proclitic after a pause, so the two halves can be identical; the mesóclise 'exterminá-los-á' is correct but bookish, and 'o Senhor, nosso Deus, os exterminará' loses the verb at the head of the colon.

options.label: os exterminará … os exterminará
options.note: Ruling: the repetition identical.

options.label: os exterminará … exterminá-los-á
options.note: MS1932's mesóclise ('destruí-los-á').

options.label: os exterminará … há de exterminá-los
options.note: the periphrastic future (as 45:6 'há de auxiliá-la').

choices.93:1: The versicle of 11-30 reads 93:1–2 as one (Sancti/11-30); nothing in the wording depends on it.
choices.93:2: Exaltáre → 'Exaltai-vos' (glossary row, which names 93:2). 'redde retributiónem' → 'pagai a retribuição', as 27:4b ('pagai-lhes a retribuição deles'); safe at the vós imperative (past 'paguei').
choices.93:3: The Latin ends 93:3 with a colon and closes the question at the end of 93:4. Each verse is chanted alone, so 93:3 closes its own question (as DRB); 93:4 is a second question. gloriári → 'gloriar-se' (glossary: the same verb for the sinners' boasting, 93:3 named).
choices.93:4: effári (φθέγγομαι, to utter) → 'proferir', kept apart from loqui → 'falar', whose repetition across the asterisk is kept. operári injustítiam → 'praticar a injustiça' (injustítia → injustiça, apart from iníquitas).
choices.93:5: Natural Portuguese order (verb first) for the Latin's fronted object 'Pópulum tuum' (D2).
choices.93:6: ádvena → 'forasteiro' (glossary; here the Greek is προσήλυτος, not πάροικος, but the Latin word is the same); pupíllus → 'órfão' (glossary).
choices.93:10: corrípere → 'castigar', árguere → 'repreender' (both settled, D21; the glossary names 93:10). sciéntia → 'o saber' (glossary names 93:10). The second colon is a relative with no main verb, as in the Latin; left hanging.
choices.93:12: erudíre → 'instruir' (glossary names 93:12); 'tu' made 'vós' explicit, as the Latin makes it explicit. The verse ends on a comma, running into 93:13, as the Latin does.
choices.93:14: repéllere → 'repelir' (settled D42); plebs → 'povo'; derelínquere → 'abandonar'. The first colon is quoted in the Invitatory (Psalterium/Invitatorium.txt, 'quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam') — Ps 94 should copy it.
choices.93:16: consúrgere → 'levantar-se'; malignántes → 'os malvados' (D24; the glossary names 93:16); 'mihi' → 'por mim' (DRB 'for me', MS1932). The second colon is long (+4): the formula 'os que praticam a iniquidade' is fixed.
choices.93:17: adjuváre → 'auxiliar' (glossary), in 93:17 and 93:18, as the Latin repeats it.
choices.93:19: Read alone as an antiphon of the Sacred Heart (Tempora/Pent02-5, TemporaM/Pent02-5) and a Lenten versicle (Quad1-4): the verse stands alone. multitúdo → 'multidão' (glossary); lætificáre → 'alegrar' (glossary names 93:19).
choices.93:22: 'factus est mihi … in refúgium' → 'se fez refúgio para mim', as 117:14 'se fez salvação para mim' (in + accusative of result, no preposition in Portuguese). The first colon is a responsory (Tempora/Epi2-5, 'R. Factus est mihi Dóminus in refúgium') and reads alone. adjutórium → 'auxílio'; spes → 'esperança'.
choices.93:23: reddere → 'pagar' (27:4b, 61:12); 'ipsórum … eórum' → 'deles … deles', so that 'sua' is not heard as the Lord's; malítia → 'malícia' (glossary names 93:23).

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps093.md (no Diurnal section for this psalm). Glossary rows read for every controlled word; finished psalms searched by Latin (ps093/conc.py). Hard readings: 93:13 'mítiges ei a diébus malis' (a compressed construction), 93:15 the verbless second colon, 93:17 nisi quia + pluperfect subjunctive, 93:20 'qui fingis labórem in præcépto' (second person, obscure), 93:6 two verbs of killing against a psalter-wide occídere → matar. Liturgical uses found by grep in content/do (Latin): 93:1–2 versicle (Sancti/11-30), 93:12 Matins versicle, 93:14a in the Invitatory, 93:19 Sacred Heart antiphon and Lenten versicle, 93:22 responsory (Epi2-5).

Hard checks pass. Soft: length +3 to +5 at 93:3b, 93:6a, 93:10a, 93:12a, 93:15b, 93:16b, 93:17a, 93:18a, 93:20a — accepted: each is a fixed formula (93:16b 'os que praticam a iniquidade'), a supplied copula or pronoun (93:12a 'vós', 93:15b 'estão'), or Portuguese's longer verb forms; none is two breaths. Short at 93:5a, 93:8a, 93:11b, 93:19b (-3/-4): the Latin's long words. No rhyme flags.
